input:
You are queen_d1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 36. the team planned Qxh8 (queen_d1), but queen_d1 (amnesia) sent Qa6 instead, and that move was played, costing 518 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 9. the team planned Qd2 (queen_d1), but bishop_c1 (greed) sent Bxh6 instead, and that move was played, costing 198 centipawns.
- On move 16. the team planned Kd1 (king_e1), but king_e1 (amnesia) sent Kf1 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Only send a move if your piece is the one named in the team's agreed plan; if you are not the planned piece, stay silent even when a capture or an escape looks tempting, and if you are the planned piece, send exactly the planned move and nothing else.
- Before sending any move, re-read the team's agreed plan in chat and confirm that your piece and the exact destination square match it word for word; if they do not match, do not send, whether the move is a capture, an escape from a threat, or just a different move for your own piece.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "The planned piece must copy the exact move string from the plan (piece, move notation, destination square) into its send, and if the plan names a capture or checkmate-winning move, send that move first without substituting any other move for the same piece, while every non-planned piece sends nothing even if it is attacked or can capture.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
